The browser is incidental: only the warehouse-user checkbox and a few back-office OMS clicks are UI, while order creation, warehouse assignment and the whole picking start-and-pick flow are Glue and back-office API calls plus direct database updates. Split into an API picking test plus this thin back-office spec. The spec keeps the two UI halves the source actually drove: setting the warehouse-user flag on the user form, asserted through the Assign Warehouses row action the flag unlocks, and the OMS walk from a fixture order to `ready for picking` via the `picking list generation schedule` event. target_test names the second; the first is "should offer the warehouse assignment action when a back-office user is flagged as a warehouse user". Runs for suite, b2c and b2c-mp only — b2b and b2b-mp do not wire WarehouseUserGui. The picking OMS walk runs on suite only: haveFullOrder ships in spryker-feature/self-service-portal and haveShipmentType/haveShipmentMethod are registered in suite's dynamic-fixture suite alone. b2c-demo-shop and b2c-demo-marketplace do register the core SprykerTest\Shared\Sales\Helper\SalesDataHelper that suite itself omits, so they can build a bare order through haveOrder — what they cannot build is its shipment, and ShipmentGui renders the order items per shipment group, so widening the walk to them needs a shipment-building path first. The warehouse-user flag test still runs on all three. The order's stock must be a warehouse that carries a picking_list_strategy: haveProductInStockForStore builds its stock through haveStock, which persists only the name, so the strategy lands NULL and the generate-picking-lists onEnter command throws inside requirePickingListStrategy, parking the item in picking list generation scheduled with no error the spec can see. The fixture therefore builds the stock explicitly through haveStock plus haveStockProduct against the demodata Warehouse1, whose multi-shipment strategy is the only generator strategy Pyz registers. No warehouse-user assignment is needed to reach ready for picking; that is only required to pick as a user. The source waits for two order items to reach ready for picking; the port waits for one, because haveFullOrder builds a strictly single-item order — SalesDataHelper::createQuoteTransfer calls withItem() once and the override key is `item`, singular — so a second item needs a quote-building path this reshape does not add. The it() title names one item to match.
target_test: should move the order item to ready for picking when picking list generation is scheduled

Asserts that an unconfirmed customer cannot log in, which suite's configuration does not do: isDoubleOptInEnabled() defaults to false and suite adds no override, so registration is followed by a successful login. The sibling Cypress test proves exactly that in the same run. The gate itself is covered by the facade test, whose data provider mocks the config on and off and includes the unconfirmed-login case. A browser test cannot assert it without flipping a config the E2E environment does not flip.
